title: Staged runtime flags and backcompat probes for structured streams
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Context: As we roll out API evolution for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs, we need a low-risk mechanism to introduce behavioral changes. This ticket implements staged runtime feature gates (behavior flags) plus automated backcompat probes that validate client-observable behavior for a representative set of workloads. Goals: (1) introduce a feature-gate framework in the serving runtime that can toggle streaming/frame semantics and tool-call boundary markers per-tenant, (2) build a probe harness that runs golden prompts against both the current and candidate behaviors and surfaces regressions, (3) wire the gating + probes into the rollout pipeline so PM/QA can approve gradual traffic ramps, and (4) add migration-checks and a short migration guide for SDK consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes feature flags at request routing layer: 'stream_frames_v2', 'tool_call_boundary_v2', 'structured_output_strict' that can be toggled per-tenant or per-route
Probe harness runs nightly and compares token-level diffs and structured schema conformance between baseline and candidate behaviors for a curated set of 200 golden prompts
If regression rate > 1% (semantic mismatch or invalid schema), candidate flag automatically stops rollout and notifies owners
Rollout UI in Console shows per-flag traffic distribution, degradation metrics (latency, token-cost, error-rate), and a one-click rollback
Migration guide (docs) published with example SDK changes, deprecation timeline, and a compatibility test command for customers
End-to-end tests added to CI that simulate streaming + tool-call interleaving and assert no silent truncation or malformed structured messages for both baseline and gated mode
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): deploy runtime with flags behind 'dev-only' gate and run probe harness against internal test tenants
Phase 1 (canary): enable flag for 1% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants, run probes every 15m, hold if regressions detected
Phase 2 (ramped): increase to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h hold windows and manual sign-off after probe pass
Fallback: automatic revert to previous behavior when probe failure threshold is breached; manual rollback via Console available at any stage
Communication: coordinate with Docs, SDK, and Customer Success; publish migration guide and deprecation calendar at Phase 1 start
test_plan: Unit tests for feature gate toggling logic and routing policy
Integration tests in CI that spin up a small cluster and run streaming+tool-call scenarios with both flag values
Probe harness: nightly job that posts results to SLO dashboard with diffs, schema-violations, and human-review queue
Load-testing for gating control-plane to ensure toggles propagate within 30s under normal load
Customer-facing compatibility test: small CLI that replays a customer's saved session against both behaviors and reports anomalies
technical_notes: Feature flags implemented as lightweight routing headers evaluated by the shard-proxy; flag state persisted in local cache seeded from central control-plane
Streaming semantics change is limited to framing and an additional 'eos_kind' token to disambiguate tool vs content ends; backwards compatible encoder path retained
Probes will compare both syntactic (JSON schema) and semantic equivalence using lightweight embedding-based similarity for structured fields
To avoid noisy alerts, probe harness will aggregate by intent-class and require consistent regression across >=3 prompts in the same class before tripping a halt
We will keep a compatibility adapter layer for SDKs that maps old streaming frames to the new framing for 6 months after full rollout
